question.text: 'Indus Global Fund', a Cat II AIF, wishes to invest in equity of an offshore VCU. Under SEBI's overseas-investment guidelines and FEMA, which of the following is correct?

answer.text: AIFs may invest in equity/equity-linked instruments of offshore VCUs (not listed in India or abroad), subject to aggregate AIF-industry limit of USD 1,500 million, allocated first-come-first-served; per-scheme cap 25% of investable funds; prior SEBI approval valid 6 months
AIFs can invest up to 50% of investable funds overseas with no aggregate industry limit
AIFs need RBI approval in addition to SEBI approval for each overseas investment
AIFs can invest in overseas JVs or WOS of the fund itself, subject to 10% cap

explanation.text: **The Logic:** Per SEBI Circular CIR/IMD/DF/7/2015 and subsequent updates: aggregate industry limit of USD 1,500 million (enhanced from USD 750 million vide May 2021 circular, n/a to IFSC Cat I/II); per-scheme cap 25% of investable funds; SEBI approval valid 6 months. Investee must be incorporated in a jurisdiction whose securities regulator is an IOSCO MMoU Appendix-A signatory OR a bilateral MoU signatory with SEBI; must not be in an FATF call-for-action jurisdiction. **The Trap:** Option B inflates the limit and drops the aggregate cap. Option C is wrong — separate RBI approval is NOT needed when SEBI approves. Option D is expressly prohibited — AIFs cannot invest in JV/WOS of themselves. **Cross-Exam Context:** XIX-C directly tests the overseas framework. XIX-A treats it as advanced. **Manager's Pro-Tip:** Manager tip: On liquidation of overseas investments, sale proceeds (to the extent of original invested amount) become available to ALL AIFs for reinvestment. Report divestment to aifreporting@sebi.gov.in within 3 working days. Only sell to entities eligible to make overseas investments under FEMA.
